concepts.name: Array
concepts.description: Fixed-size, ordered, indexable collection of same-typed elements stored contiguously in memory, supporting O(1) random access by index.

concepts.name: Rotate left array
concepts.description: Rotating an array left by k positions by concatenating slices arr[k:] + arr[:k] in O(n) time and O(n) space.

concepts.name: Reverse array
concepts.description: Reversing an array by swapping symmetric elements using two pointers moving toward the center, O(n) time, O(1) space.

concepts.name: Kadane's algorithm
concepts.description: Finding the contiguous subarray with the largest sum by maintaining the best sum ending at each position, O(n) time, O(1) space.

concepts.name: Two-pointer pair sum
concepts.description: Finding two numbers in a sorted array that sum to a target by moving left and right pointers based on comparison to target, O(n) time, O(1) space.

concepts.name: Sliding window for longest unique substring
concepts.description: Finding the longest substring without repeating characters by maintaining a hash map of last seen indices and adjusting the window start, O(n) time, O(min(n, alphabet)) space.

concepts.name: Palindrome check
concepts.description: Checking whether a string reads the same forwards and backwards by comparing characters from both ends inward, O(n) time, O(1) space.

concepts.name: Linked list
concepts.description: A linear data structure composed of nodes, each holding data and a pointer to the next node (and previous node if doubly linked).

concepts.name: Insert at head
concepts.description: Adding a new node at the head of a singly linked list by updating the node's next pointer and the list's head reference, O(1) time.

concepts.name: Reverse linked list
concepts.description: Reversing a singly linked list by iteratively rewiring each node's next pointer to point to its predecessor, O(n) time, O(1) space.

concepts.name: Floyd's cycle detection
concepts.description: Detecting a cycle in a linked list using two pointers moving at speeds of one and two steps per iteration; meeting indicates a cycle, O(n) time, O(1) space.

concepts.name: Merge sorted linked lists
concepts.description: Merging two already sorted linked lists into one sorted list by repeatedly taking the smaller head node, O(n+m) time, O(1) extra space.

concepts.name: Doubly linked list
concepts.description: A linked list where each node has both next and previous pointers, enabling traversal in both directions and O(1) removal given a node reference, and O(1) appends using a tail pointer.

concepts.name: Stack (LIFO) definition
concepts.description: A collection supporting push (add to top) and pop (remove from top) in O(1), modeling a last-in-first-out discipline.

concepts.name: Queue (FIFO) definition
concepts.description: A collection supporting enqueue (add to back) and dequeue (remove from front) in O(1), modeling a first-in-first-out discipline.

concepts.name: Stack implementation using Python list
concepts.description: Implementing a stack by wrapping Python's list to provide push/pop from the end with O(1) amortized time.

concepts.name: Bracket matching using stack
concepts.description: Checking balanced brackets in an expression by pushing opening brackets and popping to match closings, O(n) time, O(n) space.

concepts.name: Postfix expression evaluation using stack
concepts.description: Evaluating postfix (Reverse Polish) notation by pushing operands and applying operators to the top two stack values, O(n) time, O(n) space.

concepts.name: Queue implementation using collections.deque
concepts.description: Implementing a queue with O(1) enqueue/dequeue using Python's collections.deque, which provides efficient operations at both ends.

concepts.name: Circular queue implementation
concepts.description: A fixed-size queue that reuses an array as a ring buffer using modulo arithmetic for O(1) enqueue and dequeue, O(k) space.

concepts.name: MinStack
concepts.description: A stack variant that maintains a parallel min stack to provide O(1) access to the minimum element, at the cost of doubled space.

concepts.name: Recursion
concepts.description: Problem-solving pattern of reducing a problem to a smaller instance of itself with a base case termination condition; underpins sorting, tree/graph traversals, and divide-and-conquer algorithms.

concepts.name: Factorial recursion
concepts.description: Computing n! via recursive definition n! = n * (n-1)! with base case 0! = 1, O(n) time, O(n) call‑stack space.

concepts.name: Naive Fibonacci recursion
concepts.description: Computing Fibonacci numbers by recursively calling fib(n‑1) and fib(n‑2) without memoization, resulting in O(2ⁿ) time and O(n) call‑stack space.

concepts.name: Exponentiation by squaring
concepts.description: Computing baseⁿ in O(log n) time by recursively halving the exponent and squaring the intermediate result.

concepts.name: Tower of Hanoi recursion
concepts.description: Solving the Tower of Hanoi puzzle by recursively moving n‑1 disks to an auxiliary peg, moving the largest disk, then moving the n‑1 disks onto the target, requiring 2ⁿ‑1 moves (O(2ⁿ) time) and O(n) call‑stack space.

concepts.name: Linear Search
concepts.description: A search algorithm that checks each element in order until a match is found or the end is reached; works on unsorted data with O(n) time and O(1) space.

concepts.name: Binary Search
concepts.description: A search algorithm on a sorted array that repeatedly compares the target to the middle element and discards half the remaining space, achieving O(log n) time and O(1) space (iterative) or O(log n) space (recursive).

concepts.name: Search Range
concepts.description: A technique to find the first and last occurrence of a target value in a sorted array with duplicates by performing two modified binary searches that continue searching after a match; each runs in O(log n) time and O(1) space.

concepts.name: Sorting
concepts.description: The process of rearranging a collection into a defined order (e.g., ascending) to enable efficient use by other algorithms; includes comparison‑based and non‑comparison‑based methods.

concepts.name: Comparison Sort
concepts.description: A sorting algorithm that determines order solely by comparing pairs of elements; no comparison sort can beat O(n log n) worst‑case time without extra structural knowledge.

concepts.name: Bubble Sort
concepts.description: Repeatedly scans the array, swapping adjacent out‑of‑order pairs; the largest unsorted element ‘bubbles’ to its correct position each pass, with O(n²) time and O(1) space (improved to O(n) best case with early‑exit).

concepts.name: Selection Sort
concepts.description: Divides the array into a sorted prefix and unsorted suffix; each pass selects the minimum of the suffix and swaps it into the next prefix position, guaranteeing O(n²) time and O(1) space with at most n swaps.

concepts.name: Insertion Sort
concepts.description: Builds a sorted prefix one element at a time by inserting each new element into its correct position among previously sorted elements; O(n²) worst case, O(n) best case (already sorted), O(1) space.

concepts.name: Merge Sort
concepts.description: A divide‑and‑conquer sort that splits the array in half, recursively sorts each half, and merges the two sorted halves in linear time; O(n log n) time in all cases, O(n) auxiliary space.

concepts.name: Quick Sort
concepts.description: Selects a pivot, partitions the array so elements ≤ pivot are left and > pivot are right, then recursively sorts the partitions; average O(n log n) time, worst‑case O(n²), O(log n) space (stack).

concepts.name: Heap Sort
concepts.description: First builds a max‑heap from the array, then repeatedly extracts the maximum (root) and restores the heap property; O(n log n) time, O(1) extra space (in‑place).

concepts.name: Counting Sort
concepts.description: Counts occurrences of each integer in a known range [0, k] and reconstructs the output from those counts; runs in O(n + k) time and O(k) space, beating comparison‑sort limits when k is small.

concepts.name: Hash Table
concepts.description: Maps keys to values via a hash function that computes an array index; provides average‑case O(1) lookup, insertion, deletion using separate chaining (or open addressing) to resolve collisions, with O(n) worst‑case when many keys collide.

concepts.name: Two Sum
concepts.description: Finds two numbers in an unsorted array that add to a target by storing each seen number in a hash map and looking for its complement; runs in O(n) time and O(n) space.

concepts.name: Group Anagrams
concepts.description: Groups words that are anagrams by using the sorted letters of each word as a hash‑map key; runs in O(n * k log k) time and O(n * k) space for words of length up to k.

concepts.name: First Unique Character
concepts.description: Returns the index of the first character that appears exactly once in a string by building a frequency map then scanning the string in order; O(n) time and O(1) space for a bounded alphabet.

concepts.name: Tree
concepts.description: Hierarchical data structure with an ordering invariant; heaps are a specialized tree variant, and graphs generalize trees by relaxing structural constraints.

concepts.name: Binary Tree
concepts.description: A tree in which each node has at most two children, designated left and right.

concepts.name: Binary Search Tree
concepts.description: A binary tree that maintains the ordering invariant: every value in a node’s left subtree is smaller and every value in its right subtree is larger, enabling O(h) search, insertion, and deletion where h is the tree height.

concepts.name: Depth‑First Tree Traversals
concepts.description: Visits nodes by fully exploring one subtree before another; inorder (left, node, right) yields BST nodes in ascending order, preorder (node, left, right) visits parents before children, postorder (left, right, node) visits children before parents; each runs in O(n) time and O(h) space.

concepts.name: Breadth‑First Tree Traversal
concepts.description: Visits nodes level by level from top to bottom using a queue; each node is enqueued and dequeued once, giving O(n) time and O(n) worst‑case space (when a level holds Θ(n) nodes).

concepts.name: Tree Height
concepts.description: The number of edges on the longest root‑to‑leaf path; computed recursively as 1 + max(height(left), height(right)) with O(n) time and O(h) space.

concepts.name: Validate Binary Search Tree
concepts.description: Checks that a binary tree satisfies the BST ordering invariant by propagating an allowed (low, high) range down the tree; each node must lie strictly within its inherited range, yielding O(n) time and O(h) space.

concepts.name: Lowest Common Ancestor (LCA) in BST
concepts.description: Finds the deepest common ancestor of two nodes in a binary search tree by descending left or right based on BST ordering, achieving O(h) time and O(1) space.

concepts.name: Heap
concepts.description: A complete binary tree stored in an array where each parent satisfies the heap property (≤ children for min‑heap, ≥ for max‑heap), giving O(1) access to the extreme element and O(log n) insertion/deletion.

concepts.name: k‑th Largest Element via Min‑Heap
concepts.description: Maintains a min‑heap of size k while scanning numbers; the heap root after processing is the k‑th largest, running in O(n log k) time and O(k) space.

concepts.name: Merge k Sorted Lists
concepts.description: Repeatedly extracts the smallest current element from a min‑heap containing the front of each list, then pushes the next element from that list, merging in O(N log k) time and O(k) space.

concepts.name: Graph Definition and Adjacency List Representation
concepts.description: A graph consists of vertices connected by edges; an adjacency list maps each vertex to its neighbor list, using O(V+E) space and supporting directed/undirected, weighted/unweighted graphs.

concepts.name: Breadth‑First Search
concepts.description: Explores a graph layer by layer using a queue, marking visited vertices to avoid cycles; each vertex and edge processed once, yielding O(V+E) time and O(V) space.

concepts.name: Depth‑First Search
concepts.description: Recursively follows a single path before backtracking, using a visited set to prevent infinite loops in cyclic graphs; runs in O(V+E) time and O(V) space.

concepts.name: Cycle Detection in Directed Graphs
concepts.description: Detects a cycle by checking during DFS whether a neighbor is already on the current recursion stack (in_stack), with O(V+E) time and O(V) space.

concepts.name: Topological Sort
concepts.description: Repeatedly removes vertices with zero in‑degree, updating neighbors’ in‑degrees, to produce a linear ordering of a DAG; runs in O(V+E) time and O(V) space.

concepts.name: Dijkstra’s Shortest Path Algorithm
concepts.description: Finds shortest paths from a source in a weighted graph with non‑negative edges by repeatedly extracting the minimum‑distance vertex via a min‑heap and relaxing edges; O((V+E) log V) time, O(V) space.

concepts.name: Connected Components in Undirected Graphs
concepts.description: Counts components by launching a DFS/BFS from each unvisited vertex and marking all reachable vertices; each launch discovers one component, total O(V+E) time and O(V) space.

concepts.name: Dynamic Programming
concepts.description: Solves problems with optimal substructure and overlapping subproblems by solving each distinct subproblem once and storing its result (memoization or tabulation), converting exponential recursion to polynomial time.

concepts.name: Memoization
concepts.description: Uses a cache (e.g., functools.lru_cache) to store results of recursive calls so each subproblem is evaluated once; applied to Fibonacci yields O(n) time and O(n) space.

concepts.name: Tabulation
concepts.description: Iteratively fills a DP table from base cases upward, often allowing space optimisation; for Fibonacci only two rolling variables are needed, giving O(n) time and O(1) space.

concepts.name: 0/1 Knapsack Problem
concepts.description: DP table dp[i][w] stores the maximum value achievable with the first i items and capacity w; each cell computed in O(1) from prior cells, yielding O(n·W) time and space.

concepts.name: Longest Common Subsequence
concepts.description: DP table dp[i][j] gives the LCS length of prefixes; recurrence uses match or max of dropping one character, filling an (m+1)×(n+1) table in O(m·n) time and space.

concepts.name: Longest Increasing Subsequence
concepts.description: Maintains piles of smallest possible tail values for increasing subsequences of each length; each number placed via binary search, producing LIS length in O(n log n) time and O(n) space.

concepts.name: Coin Change
concepts.description: DP array dp[a] records the minimum coins needed for amount a; for each amount tries every coin, updating dp[a] = min(dp[a], dp[a‑c]+1); runs in O(amount·|coins|) time and O(amount) space.

concepts.name: Edit Distance
concepts.description: DP table dp[i][j] gives the Levenshtein distance between prefixes; initialization converts empty string to prefix via insertions/deletions; recurrence adds 1 for mismatch, yielding O(m·n) time and space.

concepts.name: Greedy Algorithm
concepts.description: Builds a solution by repeatedly picking the locally optimal choice; correct only when the problem possesses the greedy‑choice property, which must be proven.

concepts.name: Backtracking
concepts.description: Systematically explores the solution space via recursion, abandoning a path as soon as it cannot lead to a valid solution; undoes choices to try alternatives, essential for enumerating all configurations.

concepts.name: Permutation Generation via Backtracking
concepts.description: Generate all n! permutations by fixing one position at a time (recursion depth `start`), swapping each remaining element into that position, recursing on the rest, then undoing the swap (backtracking) to restore shared state for the next branch.

concepts.name: N-Queens Backtracking with Pruning
concepts.description: Place N queens on an N×N board so no two share a row, column, or diagonal. One queen per row is enforced structurally; column and diagonal conflicts are tracked with three sets, enabling O(1) conflict checks that prune entire subtrees before exploration.

concepts.name: Power Set / Subsets Generation via Backtracking
concepts.description: Generate all 2^n subsets of an n-element set. Unlike permutations, every partial path is already a valid subset, so results are recorded at every recursive call (not just at a base case), then extended by including each remaining element in turn with backtracking (pop).

concepts.name: Trie
concepts.description: A tree where each edge represents one character; root-to-node paths spell prefixes. Supports O(k) insert and lookup for a string of length k via `search` (exact word, requires is_end flag) and `starts_with` (prefix only, path existence suffices).

concepts.name: Union-Find
concepts.description: Tracks a partition of n elements into disjoint groups using a parent array. `find` follows parent pointers to the root with path compression (rewiring visited nodes directly to root). `union` merges by rank (attaching smaller tree under larger), keeping trees shallow for near-O(1) amortized operations.

concepts.name: Kruskal's MST Algorithm
concepts.description: Greedy algorithm to build a minimum spanning tree: sort all edges by weight ascending, then iterate adding an edge only if its endpoints are in different Union-Find components (union returns False when they're already connected, serving as the cycle check). Total time O(E log E) dominated by sorting.

concepts.name: Two Pointers and Sliding Window
concepts.description: Algorithmic technique using index arithmetic with two pointers or a sliding window to efficiently traverse and process sequences, reusing sorted data and search primitives.

concepts.name: Linked List Pointer Rewiring
concepts.description: Manipulating node pointers directly instead of performing index-based calculations, notably used in the merge step of merge sort.

concepts.name: Stack and Queue
concepts.description: LIFO (stack) and FIFO (queue) access disciplines underpinning call stack management and graph traversal algorithms (BFS/DFS).

concepts.name: Heap Sort / Priority Queue
concepts.description: Using a heap (weak ordering tree) to achieve O(n log n) sorting and O(log n) access to extremes (min/max); also used in Dijkstra's algorithm.

concepts.name: Graph
concepts.description: Data structure representing arbitrary pairwise connections between elements; explored via BFS/DFS traversal; Kruskal's algorithm builds a minimum spanning tree over a graph.
